annotation.title_clean: Avis sur l'usage des technologies d'intelligence artificielle par les forces armées
annotation.title_en: Opinion on the Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies by the Armed Forces
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Comité d'éthique de la défense (Ministère des Armées, France)
annotation.venue: Ministère des Armées – Comité d'éthique de la défense
annotation.summary_en: Opinion of France's Defence Ethics Committee on military use of AI, setting out 9 principles and 12 recommendations. It stresses IHL compliance, legality reviews under Article 36 AP I, testing and qualification, data sovereignty, context-dependent human decision-making, training, and human responsibility. It notes the EU AI Act excludes military AI.
key_provisions_or_claims: AI used in military operations is subject to the same legal regime as other means of warfare: IHL, the Constitution and French law.
Legality (Article 36 AP I) reviews should be adapted to AI and cover the whole lifecycle, especially identification, classification and firing functions.
AI systems must be tested, verified and validated for defined use cases and qualified in proportion to benefits and risks.
Human decision must be context-dependent and under command responsibility; the level of automation may vary; responsibility cannot be assigned to an AI system.
Military personnel need training to detect degraded AI and keep core skills; research must be free but accompanied by ethical reflection.
